text:
Jia: quick PSA — saw a spike of OOMs on p4 during multi-model soak after the kernel-selector fallback (opt->generic) landed. attaching quick notes + heap profile.

Alex: can you paste the logs / minimal repro? what models were co-resident?

Jia: repro: local runner with 3 models: llama-7b-quant, distilbert-rerank, and a tiny policy model. workload: mixed chat + embedding heavy tail. OOMs hit when a large chat request (seq=2048) landed concurrently with a batch of 8 embedding requests.

Jia: snippet from allocator high-water log:
```
[1959876543] pid=2345 alloc(activations)=7.1GB kv_cache=1.2GB workspace=512MB peak=8.9GB
[1959876551] kernel_fallback=generic (latency +8%)
[1959876552] alloc(activations)=9.8GB kv_cache=1.9GB workspace=768MB peak=11.2GB -> OOM on reserve
```

perf-bot: alert: mem_watermark increased 12% for p4-multi-model-job-42 after commit abc123; regression window 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC.

Maria: hunch: generic kernels increase per-layer workspace allocations (more temporary buffers) + our kv cache kept accumulating because small embeddings workload doesn't touch the cache TTL. two knobs to try: (1) reduce per-op max_workspace for fallback kernels, (2) add kv idle eviction during high allocation pressure.

Kevin: batch heuristics might be amplifying this — we currently let embedding batches grow to 16 during low latency windows. if activation scale ~O(batch_size * seq_len) then those concurrent batches could spike. what were batch sizes?

Jia: confirmed: embedding service auto-batched to 16, chat request was processed with seq=2048 single stream. peak math checks out.

Sam: experimented last week with soft partitioning on a dev node: gave each model a soft_vram_quota and enabled preemptive swap for models below priority=0.5. results: reduced cross-talk OOMs, but perf tail increased for preempted models. config used:
```
--runtime.soft_vram_quota="llama:9GB,distil:2GB,policy:1GB"
--swap.preemptive=true
--kv.idle_ttl=30s
--allocator.min_workspace=32MB
```

Maria: what if we combine: kernel.fallback_threshold bumped so we avoid generic if optimal kernels still pass, plus have allocator try to trim workspace on fallback and run async kv-evict when resident_mem/limit > 0.85?

Alex: can we get a microbenchmark that toggles kernel fallback and measures peak working set? I can run a quick A/B if you give me exact flags and a small script.

Jia: putting together a short repro script — will post in a minute. preliminary plan:
- run baseline (opt kernels) with autoscaling off, record high-water
- enable kernel fallback, record high-water
- enable allocator trim + kv-evict + soft quotas, record high-water
acceptance: no OOMs in 1h soak, <5% latency regression p95 for high-priority model.

Jia: repro script (pseudo):
```bash
# start three models pinned to same GPU
run_model --model llama-7b --port 7001 --priority=1 --soft_quota=9GB &
run_model --model distilbert --port 7002 --priority=0.6 --soft_quota=2GB &
run_model --model policy-small --port 7003 --priority=0.1 --soft_quota=1GB &
# generator load: one long-chat every 2s (seq=2048)
# embedding load: poisson mean 0.5s, batch up to 16
# toggles: --kernel.fallback_threshold=0.85 --allocator.trim_on_fallback=true --kv.idle_evict=true
```

perf-bot: perf test job queued: job/1959876543-abtest (ETA 18m).

Kevin: one gotcha — trimming workspace aggressively can blow up kernel execution because some optimized kernels rely on temp buffers; we should set a floor (min_workspace) and log metrics when trimming occurs.

Maria: agree. propose defaults for experiment: allocator.min_workspace=32MB, allocator.trim_pct=25% on fallback, kv.idle_ttl=20s, soft_vram_preempt_threshold=0.9.

Alex: i'll run A/B later today. assign me to run no-evict vs evict runs.

Sam: i'll spin a dev node with soft quotas and the preemptive swap. can we also add a metric that counts "kv-evict-by-pressure" events?

Jia: yes — add metric and an alert: if kv-evict-by-pressure > 0 and p95_latency(high_prio) increases > 15% then rollback.

Maria: canary plan: roll to 5% of fleet with soft quotas + kv-evict + allocator trim, monitor mem_watermark, OOM count, and p95 for high_prio routes for 2h window.

Alex: noted. i'll paste results here once runs finish (expect ~30-40m per run).

Jia: thanks all — main action items: Alex (A/B runs), Sam (dev node + soft quota), Maria (canary config + dashboard), Kevin (watch kernel safety floor). i'll follow up with logs and the trimmed heap profiles. :thumbsup:
